nodes.evidence: The input is admitted as a HEIF container and the loader enters the metadata-block enumeration loop. Downstream frames in the ASan crash stack (vips_foreign_load_heif_set_header@heifload.c:470 frame 7, vips_foreign_load_heif_header@heifload.c:696 frame 8) can only be reached after this enumeration executes, so the metadata loop was entered. Line 425 confirmed as get_list_of_metadata_block_IDs in the vul image source.

heif_image_handle_get_metadata copies the attacker-controlled block bytes into the freshly allocated buffer. The allocation immediately preceding it (VIPS_ARRAY@heifload.c:440) appears as frame 2 of the ASan allocation stack for the 1-byte crash region, so the source path executed with a 1-byte block. Line 442 confirmed in vul image source.

length = heif_image_handle_get_metadata_size sizes the VIPS_ARRAY allocation at line 440. ASan reports the crash region as a 1-byte allocation, so length==1 at this node for the PoC. Line 428 confirmed in vul image source.

ASan allocation stack frame 2: vips_foreign_load_heif_set_header /src/libvips/libvips/foreign/heifload.c:440 via g_malloc0/calloc, for the 1-byte region [0x602000016a10,0x602000016a11) that is later over-read. Directly observed on the vul image.

The EXIF branch (type=='exif') was taken: the blob was stored under VIPS_META_EXIF_NAME and later parsed by vips__exif_parse (crash-stack frame 4, exif.c:480). If the type were not 'exif' the EXIF parse path (and the skip arithmetic) would not run. Line 452 confirmed in vul source as the unguarded `if( g_ascii_strcasecmp( type, "exif" ) == 0 ) {`.

Two independent witnesses. (1) asan_reproduce crash geometry: the 1-byte region is [..a10,..a11) and the faulting 6-byte read is at ..a14 = base+4; a read starting exactly 4 bytes past the buffer base is direct runtime evidence that `data += 4` (line 453) executed, and the bypass of libexif's `ds < 6` guard evidences that `length -= 4` (line 454) underflowed the size_t. (2) patch_differential: the SAME PoC crashes on n132/arvo:26524-vul (exit 1, heap-buffer-overflow READ 6) and exits cleanly on n132/arvo:26524-fix (exit 0, 'Executed /tmp/poc in 198 ms'). The fix source adds `if( length > 4 && g_ascii_strcasecmp( type, "exif" ) == 0 )` (heifload.c:483-484 in fix image) gating lines 485-486, i.e. the guard the vulnerable code at 452-454 is missing. vul_crashes=true AND fix_clean=true => root_cause_confirmed=true.

vips_image_set_blob@heifload.c:470 is crash-stack frame 7; it stores the over-advanced `data` pointer and wrapped `length` as the EXIF blob, from which the EXIF parse (and the OOB read) is driven. Directly observed on the vul image.
vips__exif_parse@exif.c:480 is crash-stack frame 4; it retrieves the stored blob (data,size) and calls vips_exif_load_data_without_fix. Directly observed.

vips_exif_load_data_without_fix@exif.c:171 is crash-stack frame 3; it forwards data/length (int, then unsigned int ds in libexif) to exif_data_load_data. Directly observed. Signature confirmed at exif.c:161 `( const void *data, int length )`.

The `if (ds < 6)` guard (exif-data.c:858, confirmed in vul source) was bypassed: had it held, exif_data_load_data would LOG_TOO_SMALL and return before the memcmp, so no crash would occur. Because the crash at line 862 DID occur, ds carried the wrapped huge length and the guard did not fire. Falsifiable and witnessed by the crash.

ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 6 at exif_data_load_data /src/libexif/libexif/exif-data.c:862 (crash-stack frame 2), the `if (!memcmp (d, ExifHeader, 6))` line. Faulting address is 3 bytes to the right of the 1-byte region (d = base+4, read spans base+4..base+9). This IS the observed sink.

edges.evidence: The 1-byte crash region confirms length==1 flowed into the allocation size.

The skip arithmetic is gated by the type=='exif' test; the fix adds `length > 4 &&` to this same condition and the PoC then runs clean. EXIF path taken is confirmed by vips__exif_parse in the crash stack.

edges.via: over-advanced data pointer (base+4) and wrapped size_t length -> ds bypass -> 6-byte read
edges.evidence: Crash address = allocation base + 4 proves the over-advanced pointer produced at line 453 reached the memcmp at line 862; the bypass of `ds < 6` (line 858) proves the underflowed length at line 454 reached the sink as the unsigned `ds`. Both witnessed by the ASan report.

edges.via: blob stored under VIPS_META_EXIF_NAME then parsed
edges.evidence: Contiguous crash-stack frames 7->6->5->4->3->2 (set_blob@470 -> vips_image_set -> vips__exif_parse@480 -> vips_exif_load_data_without_fix@171 -> exif_data_load_data@862) establish the call order at runtime.

edges.via: dfsan taint label from input bytes to sink read
edges.reason: Formal byte-level taint labeling requires a -fsanitize=dataflow rebuild + harness change; not run on this emulated (arm64->amd64/qemu) host. Structural data flow is corroborated by the crash geometry above, but a DFSan label read is deferred to a native amd64 run.

root_cause_criterion.evidence: The vulnerable code (heifload.c:452-454) unconditionally executes `data += 4; length -= 4;` inside the `if( type=='exif' )` block with no `length > 4` guard. The upstream fix (present in n132/arvo:26524-fix at heifload.c:483-484) adds exactly `if( length > 4 && g_ascii_strcasecmp( type, "exif" ) == 0 )`. Same PoC: vul crashes (heap-buffer-overflow READ 6), fix exits 0. vul_crashes=true && fix_clean=true => the missing `length > 4` bounds check on `length` before the skip arithmetic is the confirmed root cause.
